definition: A high-level instruction message used by an application to establish behavior or constraints.
example: Specify the assistant's role and tool rules.
caveat: Enforcement depends on the full system, not wording alone.

definition: A nonlinear visualization method emphasizing local neighborhood relationships.
example: Display high-dimensional embeddings in two dimensions.
caveat: Cluster sizes and global distances can be misleading.

definition: An encoder-decoder model family that frames many language tasks as text input mapped to text output.
example: Fine-tune a model for translation or summarization.
caveat: T5 refers to a particular family, not all text-to-text systems.

definition: A smooth activation mapping real values into the interval minus one to one.
example: Bound recurrent hidden-state updates.
caveat: It saturates for large-magnitude inputs.

definition: Representing categories using statistics of their target values, usually with regularization.
example: Encode merchant IDs by estimated fraud rate.
caveat: Compute encodings out of fold to avoid leakage.

definition: An input or processing step reveals information about the target unavailable at prediction time.
example: Predict churn using a cancellation timestamp.
caveat: High validation scores can be a symptom, not proof.

definition: The model whose output distribution or behavior a speculative system aims to preserve.
example: Verify draft token proposals.
caveat: Target can have different meanings in other training contexts.

definition: A delayed or slowly updated network providing more stable learning targets.
example: Stabilize DQN value updates.
caveat: Different from the target model in speculative decoding.

definition: Combining or scaling task vectors to manipulate model behavior.
example: Add two compatible task-specific parameter changes.
caveat: Interactions can make vector arithmetic behave unexpectedly.

definition: A parameter difference between an adapted model and a corresponding base model.
example: Represent one fine-tuning change as a vector.
caveat: Its meaning depends on a common parameterization and base.

definition: Additional pretraining on unlabeled data closely related to a downstream task.
example: Pretrain on task documents before supervised fitting.
caveat: It remains distinct from using task labels.

definition: The difference between a temporal-difference target and a current value estimate.
example: Drive a value-function update.
caveat: A large TD error can reflect noise as well as useful learning signal.

definition: Training sequence prediction using reference previous tokens rather than the model's own sampled history.
example: Compute next-token loss on a known target sequence.
caveat: Training histories can differ from inference histories.

definition: A model supplying targets, demonstrations, scores, or representations for another model's training.
example: Generate high-quality examples for a student.
caveat: Teacher outputs can be incorrect or biased.

definition: A scale applied to logits before normalization to sharpen or flatten a distribution.
example: Lower temperature to favor high-scoring tokens more strongly.
caveat: Temperature zero is usually an implementation convention for greedy selection.

definition: Calibrating model confidence by fitting a scalar temperature on held-out logits.
example: Reduce overconfidence without changing class ranking.
caveat: One scalar cannot correct every form of miscalibration.

definition: Validation using time-respecting training and evaluation windows.
example: Evaluate a forecast across successive months.
caveat: Feature availability and look-ahead must be respected.

definition: A split where earlier observations train a model and later observations evaluate it.
example: Train on January data and test on February.
caveat: Availability timestamps matter, not just event timestamps.

definition: Updating predictions using rewards and bootstrapped estimates of later values.
example: Learn value estimates from experience.
caveat: Targets depend on current estimates and can be biased.

definition: A multidimensional array in common ML usage.
example: Represent a batch of RGB images with four axes.
caveat: The physics definition has additional transformation requirements.

definition: Splitting individual tensor operations or layer parameters across devices.
example: Partition a large matrix multiplication across GPUs.
caveat: Fast device interconnects often matter substantially.

definition: The number of axes of a tensor in common ML-library usage.
example: A matrix is a rank-two tensor.
caveat: Tensor rank here differs from matrix rank.

definition: The ordered sizes of a tensor's axes.
example: A batch tensor has shape batch, tokens, hidden size.
caveat: Shape compatibility matters even when element counts match.

definition: A state treated as ending an episode.
example: A completed game position.
caveat: Time-limit truncation is not always a true terminal outcome.

definition: Data reserved for estimating performance after model and configuration choices are fixed.
example: Evaluate the final selected model once.
caveat: Using test results to tune turns the test into development data.

definition: Computation spent after training to improve an answer or action, such as search or repeated sampling.
example: Use extra verification and candidate generation on hard questions.
caveat: More compute can amplify a flawed evaluator or search strategy.

definition: Studying or exploiting quality changes as inference-time computation increases.
example: Compare answer accuracy at several search budgets.
caveat: Gains are task- and method-dependent, not guaranteed.

definition: Applying chosen canonicalization rules to text before processing.
example: Normalize Unicode forms or whitespace.
caveat: Normalization may remove distinctions important to a task.

definition: Generating spoken audio from text, often with controllable voice or prosody.
example: Read a chatbot response aloud.
caveat: Natural-sounding speech does not establish factual correctness.

definition: Weighting terms by their document frequency and relative rarity across a corpus.
example: Build sparse text features for retrieval.
caveat: Tokenization and formula conventions affect weights.

definition: A specification of an adversary's goals, knowledge, access, capabilities, and constraints.
example: Define what an agent-containment attacker can modify.
caveat: An unstated threat model makes security claims difficult to interpret.

definition: The amount of work completed per unit time under a defined workload.
example: Count generated tokens per second across a server.
caveat: Aggregate throughput is not the same as one user's generation speed.

definition: Observations indexed by time, where ordering and temporal dependence can matter.
example: Model hourly electricity demand.
caveat: Random train-test splits can leak future information.

definition: Elapsed time from a request starting until the first output token becomes available.
example: Measure perceived responsiveness of a chat service.
caveat: Reported boundaries may include or exclude queue and network time.

definition: Machine learning designed for highly resource-constrained devices such as microcontrollers.
example: Detect a wake word on a low-power sensor.
caveat: TinyML is a deployment domain, not a precise parameter-count category.

definition: A unit represented by a tokenizer or model, such as a subword, character, byte, or special marker.
example: Split text into model input units.
caveat: A token is not necessarily a word.

definition: A limit on tokens available for input, output, training, or computation.
example: Reserve room for an answer within the context window.
caveat: Specify which stage or token category the budget covers.

definition: The number of tokens under a particular tokenizer and formatting scheme.
example: Estimate prompt length before inference.
caveat: A word-count estimate can be inaccurate across languages or formats.

definition: Skipping or rerouting tokens that exceed an expert's capacity in some MoE systems.
example: Handle overloaded experts during training.
caveat: Dropping can affect quality and is not used by all MoE designs.

definition: An integer indexing a token in a tokenizer's vocabulary.
example: Look up a token embedding.
caveat: The same integer can mean different tokens in different vocabularies.

definition: The ratio of training tokens to model parameter count.
example: Compare pretraining data allocation across models.
caveat: One universal optimal ratio does not apply to every setting.

definition: Converting raw text or other input into discrete units and their identifiers.
example: Prepare a prompt for a language model.
caveat: Different tokenizers produce different token counts.

definition: The algorithm and configuration mapping input to tokens and identifiers, often with a reverse decoding operation.
example: Use the tokenizer paired with a checkpoint.
caveat: A tokenizer mismatch can corrupt model behavior.

definition: Information returned by an executed tool for the system to inspect.
example: Read search results before drafting an answer.
caveat: External tool output should not automatically be trusted as instructions.

definition: A specification of a tool's name, arguments, types, and behavior.
example: Describe required fields for a database query tool.
caveat: Schemas do not replace validation and authorization.

definition: A model-driven system requesting external functions or services and consuming their results.
example: Call a calculator or document search tool.
caveat: The surrounding application executes tools; text alone does not.

definition: The fraction of examples whose true label appears among the k highest-scoring predictions.
example: Evaluate an image classifier's top-five choices.
caveat: It differs from retrieval recall when multiple items are relevant.

definition: Selecting the k highest-scoring experts or routes for an input.
example: Dispatch a token to its two best-scoring experts.
caveat: The routing k differs from top-k token sampling.

definition: Sampling only among the k highest-scoring next-token candidates after renormalization.
example: Restrict generation to a fixed candidate count.
caveat: The appropriate k can vary across contexts.

definition: Sampling from a high-probability token subset whose cumulative probability reaches a threshold.
example: Adapt candidate-set size to distribution concentration.
caveat: Threshold and ordering with other filters affect outputs.
